sections.en: WTI Crude Oil is changing hands near $93.53, -6.75% over the past 24 hours and -8.73% on a 7-day view. Spot trades above the 50-day average ($89.28) and above the 200-day average ($79.47), keeping the medium-term structure constructive. The 30-day tape reads as a recovery phase (+19.63%), suggesting the market is still repairing.

sections.en:
**Trend structure.** Across horizons the picture is mixed — the moving averages are interleaved rather than stacked, which is characteristic of a transitional or range-bound regime rather than a one-way trend. Spot at $93.53 versus EMA20 $94.69, EMA50 $89.28 and EMA200 $79.47 frames the medium-term bias mechanically rather than emotionally. From this configuration the desk's working assumption is that trend-following exposure is only justified while price holds the side of the 50-day average it currently occupies.

**Key levels.** The operational map reads: initial support at $93.03 (recent swing low); the lower Bollinger band $78.00 as the 2σ downside envelope; first resistance at $96.05 (recent swing high); upper band $108.33 as the stretch target. Levels derived from the last ~60 sessions of closes are guides for location, not promises of reaction; they mark where prior two-way business was done and therefore where resting liquidity is most plausible. ATR(14) of $4.449 implies a typical daily range of roughly 4.8 percent of spot, which is the unit of risk to size positions against.

**Momentum.** RSI(14) prints 51.2 — neutral territory; MACD (12/26/9) sits above its signal line (4.376 vs 4.348, histogram +0.02807), consistent with building momentum. Momentum readings are state descriptors, not trade signals on their own; the desk treats confluence between momentum and level location as the actionable unit.

**Volatility & liquidity.** 30-day realized volatility annualizes near 53%; the 20-day band spans 33% of the mid — expanded, which favors trend continuation tactics; 7-day turnover runs at 1.17x the trailing-month norm. Behavior around these regimes — absorption at band edges, volume confirmation on breaks — is what separates a tradeable move from noise.

**Performance context.** On longer windows the asset has returned +19.63% over 30 days and -8.47% over 90 days. Positioning decisions made on monthly horizons should respect these base rates instead of extrapolating the last week. The 7-session change (-8.73%) is the shortest window the desk treats as signal rather than noise.

sections.en:
**Bullish scenario.** Continuation higher requires acceptance above $96.05 on expanding turnover; continued holds of the 50-day average ($89.28). Under those conditions the path of least resistance flips to buy-the-dip, with prior resistance converting to support as the confirmation test.

**Bearish scenario.** Downside continuation triggers on a decisive loss of $93.03. In that case failed support typically becomes the new ceiling, and momentum chasers provide the exit liquidity.

Net take on WTI Crude Oil: spot $93.53 with the medium-term bias constructive while price holds the relevant side of the 50-day average. The 24-hour tape (-6.75%) is consistent with that bias. Decision zones are the levels named in the technical section, not opinions: trade the reaction at those prices, not the headline of the day.
